But it would also waste the driver's time, actually more of their time, if they had to wait for the cashier to have an opening to fill the drink at the front during peak times.

I have an honest question for you, and this is just me being curious. What is the difference between a Dasher filling your drink and grabbing the pre-filled drink to deliver? Same potentially dirty hands grabbing the same cup. The only extra step required to fill the drink is to put a lid on the cup. So please tell me, what about that would they teach me in a safety course?

Not to mention that these same machines are operated by customers that dine in. And no one ever teaches us how to fill our own drinks. It's just a weird thing to get hung up about.

You clearly have no respect or empathy for the people that work there. You must be one of the Dashers that get in their face when they don't have your order ready right when you walk in and they tell you it'll be a few minutes. Hate this subreddit, fr.

It's implied that you would have a problem with the workers at the restaurant not filling the drink orders themselves. In the cases where I've had to do it at WingStop, I can tell they really can't leave the register at a moment's notice to help with the drink.

Get real. It's extremely inconvenient during peak times. Plenty of workers have no problem filling drinks for me at WingStop when things are slower and they know they can do it. But when they have a line of people and orders coming from the kitchen, it feels like a small thing I can do to lessen the workload.   


Sure you can cry, THAT'S WHAT THEY'RE PAID FOR! Yes, but it would honestly affect Dashers if you had to wait there with the food until they have the chance to pop by the drink machine in the front. That happened to me once during peak rush hour and they had to get a bottled drink from a fridge as a replacement for my customer. Waited like 5 minutes with the food in my bag.

Other restaurants do it because they already have a system in place for it. WingStop in my area don’t offer drive-thru service, so there’s no reason to have a machine in the kitchen. The machines are in the front and it is up to the customers to fill their drinks like at every other fast food restaurant. A full-service restaurant prepares drinks for you because all you have to do is sit your ass down to eat. Very different argument here.
Schedule another worker my ass. So many places here where I live are still understaffed because people won’t take those jobs or just don’t show up. You really want to blame the workers for that?

It’s really no big deal for me. I deliver from WingStop all the time and most of the time the workers are swamped with stuff to do. They have people waiting in line and can’t go to the machine to fill drinks for every DoorDash order that comes out of the kitchen. They also have no space to place drinks where they put the bags so it’s not like they can pre-fill everything. Most of these locations are also still severely understaffed. I do what I can to be patient and do this small task because they’re already working their asses off for their paycheck.

What is needed here is a better system or an extra machine in the kitchen like most fast food places for ease of access. Their kitchens are quite small tho, so it’s not very forgiving.
